clue.text: Athletic feats which may impress the field

definitions.text: Athletic feats which may impress the field

parts.words: Athletic feats which may impress the field
parts.note: gymnastic sideways wheelings over the hands, which could leave hand-prints pressed into a grassy field

explanation.surface: Sporting achievements that might wow a crowd of fielders or competitors.
explanation.definitionFit: These are acrobatic sideways rotations on hands and feet, a classic display of gymnastic agility.

clue.text: Century not recorded, though he beat the Indians

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a broadcast that is not recorded goes out live

explanation.surface: A cricketer who missed a hundred off the record but still defeated an Indian side.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Clive, 'Clive of India', won the Battle of Plassey in 1757; the cricket picture of a century and India is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Clive led East India Company forces to victory at Plassey over the Nawab of Bengal.

clue.text: To arrange samples etc, haphazardly is a modern twist

indicators.note: a twist given to the words is a modern scrambles their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that shuffling samples at random is a recent fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' rearranges ISAMODERN.
explanation.definitionFit: To randomise a sample is to order it by chance so no selection bias creeps in.

clue.text: Serpent, for example, scaled by Beaufort?

definitions.text: Serpent, for example, scaled by Beaufort?

parts.words: Serpent, for example, scaled by Beaufort?
parts.note: the serpent is an old bass horn; the Beaufort scale grades the force of moving air, so a device it measures plays on both senses

explanation.surface: A snake whose scales were counted by someone named Beaufort.
explanation.walkthrough: The serpent is an S-shaped wooden horn of the 16th to 19th centuries; Admiral Beaufort devised the scale of breeze strengths, so 'scaled' turns from snake skin to a measuring scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A serpent is a blown musical device, one of the horn family played with breath.

clue.text: Nature of French drivers

definitions.meaning: the intrinsic character or core of something
in France motorists fill up with this word, the French for petrol

explanation.definitionFit: The core quality of a thing is its nature, and in French the same word names petrol, what drivers buy.

clue.text: Highball before lamb, say, can be a bloomer

indicators.note: before puts the high ball ahead of the lamb in the answer

parts.note: a lob is a ball hit or thrown high
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A tall drink before a lamb dish can make you blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highball' looks like the cocktail, and 'bloomer' like a mistake; it is a flowering plant. Charles Lamb signed his Essays of Elia with that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a garden flower, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Powder found in hospital cabinets?

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the run of the words hospital cabinets

explanation.surface: Asking whether powder is kept in hospital cupboards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' points to hospiTAL Cabinets.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral ground into a fine dusting powder.

clue.text: Greek take-away counters?

parts.note: bead frames used for subtraction sums, whose name comes from a Greek word for a counting board, not a Greek restaurant's tills

explanation.surface: The tills in a Greek takeaway restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take-away' suggests food, but it means subtraction; the counting frame's name comes from Greek abax.
explanation.definitionFit: These are bead frames for arithmetic, the plural of the Latin-Greek name for the counting device.

clue.text: Keen, having gone off to endless ice-making — or some such work

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry in grief

indicators.note: food gone off is spoiled, so the word gone is jumbled
endless means the word ice loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone eager who left for an icy job of freezing work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' scrambles GONE to OGEN and 'endless' cuts ICE to IC. 'ice-making' runs on from the wordplay into the definition, the clue's whole tail describing low-temperature work.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes producing or working at extremely low temperatures, as in freezing processes.

clue.text: He holds back a strip cartoon that is funny, right to the end

indicators.note: to the end puts the right letter after the rearranged letters
funny means odd, so the words a strip cartoon are muddled

explanation.surface: A man who keeps back a comic strip that is amusing until the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges ASTRIPCARTOON into PROCRASTINATO, and 'to the end' adds R.
explanation.definitionFit: A delayer who keeps putting tasks off is one who holds back from doing them.

clue.text: Time for taking deliveries of new gin in taverns

indicators.note: in puts the reworked gin inside the taverns

parts.note: inns are taverns

indicators.note: new means the letters of gin are made into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Time spent taking in deliveries of fresh gin at pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns GIN into ING. Deliveries are bowled balls in cricket, so a batting side's turn is the time for receiving them.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a side's batting turn is when it faces the bowlers' balls.

clue.text: Nursery-rhyme scholarship

parts.note: a student grant whose name rhymes with the word nursery, not learned study of children's verses

explanation.surface: Academic study of children's verses.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like the study of children's songs, but asks for a grant whose name rhymes with 'nursery'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bursary is a grant of money to fund a student's studies.

clue.text: Moving in too lame a fashion

indicators.note: in too lame a fashion signals the words in too lame put into a new shape

explanation.surface: Walking in a way that is far too limp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a fashion' rearranges INTOOLAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moving stirs the feelings, which is what this adjective means.

clue.text: Centre-piece of lucky heather needs stick

indicators.note: the centre-piece of a word is its middle letter, here from lucky

parts.note: ling is a common name for heather

explanation.surface: The middle sprig of lucky heather has to be glued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre-piece of' takes C from luCky. Sprigs of white heather are sold as lucky charms in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to adhere, holding fast as glue does.

clue.text: Highest mark by girl is incorrect

parts.note: A is the top grade in marking
a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: Top grade awarded to a girl is a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone wrong or faulty is awry, which the adverb-adjective expresses.

clue.text: Lancaster's make-up inherited from his forefathers

indicators.note: the make-up of a word is the letters of Lancaster rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: The character of a Lancaster comes down from his family line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' rearranges LANCASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Passed down by the family line from earlier generations, as a heritage would be.

clue.text: Derivation of English mother-race

parts.note: ma is mother
a nation is a race or people

explanation.surface: The origin of the English mother tongue among peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that issues or flows out from a source is derived from it, an outpouring.

clue.text: Arrangement of nine sound whispers

indicators.note: an arrangement of the words nine sound puts their letters into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A musical arrangement of nine notes that sound like whispering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement of' rearranges NINESOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Insinuations are hinted remarks, whispered suggestions of something discreditable.

clue.text: Sort of sale given the go-ahead?

definitions.meaning: a sell-off of remaining stock at reduced prices

explanation.definitionFit: A stock sell-off is one kind of sale, and official permission, as for a plane to take off, is another sense.

clue.text: Strange American city publication

parts.note: novel means new and unusual
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: An odd publication from an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: A short novel is a published work of fiction.

clue.text: Cuts in middle of week bring black-out

indicators.note: in places the cuts inside the middle of week
the middle of week is its central two letters

parts.note: clips are cuts

explanation.surface: Cuts in midweek lead to a power failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes EE from wEEk, and 'in' puts CLIPS between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclipse blocks out the light of the sun or moon, a darkening.

clue.text: A note from the doctor?

definitions.meaning: the keynote, the first degree of a musical scale
a restorative medicine a doctor might prescribe

explanation.definitionFit: The keynote of a musical scale is a note, and a pick-me-up medicine is something a doctor gives.

clue.text: 3 dn, for example, a wash-out with Head of Music

indicators.note: wash-out says the word wash is knocked out of shape
the head of Music is its first letter

explanation.surface: A wind instrument is a failure with a music director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges WASH into SHAW; 'Head of' gives M.
explanation.definitionFit: The shawm is a medieval reed instrument, played by blowing, so an example of the instrument at 3 down.

clue.text: He has his lines to get on with

definitions.text: He has his lines to get on with

parts.words: He has his lines to get on with
parts.note: a performer who must learn a script before going on stage

explanation.surface: A man with tasks or a queue he has to tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get on' means go on stage, and 'lines' are a script.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage performer speaks scripted lines in a role.

clue.text: Soldier to offer information unasked

definitions.meaning: a person who enlists in the forces of their own accord
to put forward facts without being asked

explanation.definitionFit: An unpaid enlisted soldier is one sense, and to proffer information freely is the verb.

clue.text: Planes going up making rackets?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Planes' are flat surfaces, not aircraft, and 'rackets' are rip-offs, not tennis bats.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclined surfaces leading upward are slopes, and in British slang a swindle or overcharge is this word.

clue.text: A genuine case for money, connected with an image-converter

indicators.note: the genuine word forms a case around the money

parts.note: real means genuine
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: A real case for cash relating to a device that turns pictures into signals.
explanation.walkthrough: The image-converter is the retina, which turns light into nerve signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the eye's light-sensitive layer, which turns images into nerve signals.

clue.text: This conference-centre has much money to hold back

parts.note: pots of money is a lot of it
to dam is to hold back water

explanation.surface: A venue that has a great deal of cash to keep in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: The Potsdam Conference of 1945 settled post-war Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The German city hosted the 1945 Allied summit on post-war Europe.

clue.text: Spree, perhaps, for long-boat of old

parts.note: Noah's ark is the boat of old

explanation.surface: The German river Spree as a possible route for an ancient longboat.
explanation.walkthrough: Spree looks like the Berlin river, but it is a fling or bit of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A spree is a bit of fun or escapade, which this word means too.

clue.text: Vocational self-caterers?

parts.note: people who pursue their working life to serve their own interests

explanation.surface: People on a working holiday who cook for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambitious people who put advancing in their profession above all serve their own interests through their work.
